$comment: ENGINE-WIDE defaults for per-story budgets. A project overrides any of these in its own llm-settings.json and need not restate the rest. These are the knobs an operator reaches for when a run burns its budget or a model truncates its answer — they were literals inside a case statement in a 10,000-line shell script, changeable only by editing code.

generator.description: a generator writes one large artefact in few turns — the inverse budget of an implementer

outputTokenFloors.$comment: Minimum output budget raised at specific steps that must not be truncated. Applied as a floor: the larger of the tier budget and this value wins.

$whyOutputCaps: Raised 2026-09-21 (regintel run 140717Z): medium/high were 6144, and z-ai/glm-5.3 returned exactly 6144 output tokens on every iteration of REGI-003b and REGI-004-A — truncated mid-answer, so the runner ended with no result (raw=0 bytes) and the ladder retried the identical cap seven times. A cap must leave a reasoning model comfortable room to finish an answer; 32768 is within every set's models' output limits.

timeouts.$comment: ENGINE-WIDE walls. A project overrides any of these in its own llm-settings.json; one that declares none inherits these, as with effortTiers. Added 2026-09-22: the loader read timeouts from the project only, so regintel — which declares none — fell back to literals written in story-watchdog.sh (600/1200/2400/900) and REGI-003b died twice at 600s having read a 369-line test file and planned inside the same budget.

storyEffortTimeoutSecs.$comment: Per-effort floor for ONE attempt; the effective wall is derived from the attempt's own iteration budget (secondsPerIteration x maxIterations + perAttemptOverheadSecs) and capped at storyTimeoutMaxSecs. A floor exists so an attempt is never killed for being slower than the cheapest story in the phase.
